title: Equality of kernels on filtered cycle representatives
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be abelian [def-sp-abelian], $K$ a cochain complex, and $F$ a decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration]. Fix $p,n,r\in\mathbf Z$ with $r\ge1$ and $B_r\le Z_r$ as in [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Set $S=F^pK/F^{p+r}K$, $T=F^{p-r+1}K/F^{p+1}K$, and $R=F^pK^n\cap d^{-1}(F^{p+r}K^{n+1})$, viewed inside $F^pK^n$. For any $\varphi:S\to T$ commuting with the quotient projections and the inclusion $F^pK\to F^{p-r+1}K$, and any $z:R\to Z_r$ and $g:R\to Z^n(S)$ whose composites with the respective inclusions are the graded and quotient projections of $R$, the two maps $R\xrightarrow{z}Z_r\to Z_r/B_r$ and $R\xrightarrow{g}Z^n(S)\to H^n(S)\xrightarrow{H^n(\varphi)}H^n(T)$ have equal kernel subobjects of $R$. No epimorphism hypothesis on $z$ or $g$ is needed.

proof.text: The supplied projection square and the cycle lift equation imply g ≫ cyclesMap(phi) ≫ T.iCycles = R.arrow followed by the inclusion F^p → F^(p-r+1) and the quotient projection to T. This follows from cyclesMap_i and evaluating the projection square in degree n.

proof.text: For B ≤ Z, the kernel of coker(B → Z) is the pullback of B along Z.arrow. Indeed, a morphism a into Z is killed by this cokernel iff it lifts through B → Z (the abelian mono-cokernel kernel property), iff a ≫ Z.arrow factors through B. Pulling back along z and using the supplied equation for z identifies the first kernel with the pullback of B along R.arrow followed by the graded projection.

proof.text: Apply the boundary pullback calculation [lem-sp-filtered-complex-boundary-pullback] and then pull back along R.arrow. It identifies the first kernel with the pullback of ker(T.pOpcycles n) along the representative map R → T^n.

proof.text: Kernels are unchanged after postcomposition by the mono T.homologyι n. Homology projection naturality and homology_π_ι identify the second map followed by this mono with g ≫ cyclesMap(phi) ≫ T.iCycles n ≫ T.pOpcycles n. The first step identifies this composite with the representative map R → T^n followed by pOpcycles. Pullback of a kernel is the kernel of the composite (pullback_equalizer). Consequently the two kernels coincide.

lean.statement:
theorem filteredComplex_representative_kernels (F : DecreasingFiltration K)
    (p n r : ℤ) (hr : 1 ≤ r)
    (hBZ : F.complexBoundaries p n r ≤ F.complexCycles p n r)
    (ha : p - r + 1 ≤ p) (hb : p + 1 ≤ p + r) :
    let hs := (Int.le_add_one (show p ≤ p from le_rfl)).trans hb
    let ht := ha.trans (Int.le_add_one (show p ≤ p from le_rfl))
    let R := F.complexCycleRepresentatives p n r
    let Z := F.complexCycles p n r
    let B := F.complexBoundaries p n r
    let S := F.complexQuotient p (p + r) hs
    let T := F.complexQuotient (p - r + 1) (p + 1) ht
    ∀ (φ : S ⟶ T),
      F.complexQuotientπ p (p + r) hs ≫ φ =
        Subobject.ofLE (F.step p) (F.step (p - r + 1)) (F.antitone_step ha) ≫
          F.complexQuotientπ (p - r + 1) (p + 1) ht →
      ∀ (z : (R : C) ⟶ (Z : C)) (g : (R : C) ⟶ S.cycles n),
        z ≫ Z.arrow = R.arrow ≫
          (F.complexQuotientπ p (p + 1) (Int.le_add_one (show p ≤ p from le_rfl))).f n →
        g ≫ S.iCycles n = R.arrow ≫ (F.complexQuotientπ p (p + r) hs).f n →
        kernelSubobject (z ≫ cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE B Z hBZ)) =
          kernelSubobject (g ≫ S.homologyπ n ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap φ n)
